- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is consistently below recent highs, adjust upward by 2–5% to capture bullish momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong downward trend + low sentiment, add a 3–5% downward bias to avoid false recovery.  
- If forecast overshoots true value by >5% in early days (e.g., day 1–5), apply a 2–3% downward correction to prevent overconfidence in short-term momentum.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating between 0.3–0.7) and forecast is erratic, smooth the curve by averaging adjacent days’ predictions.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome shows mean reversion toward 65–70 range after a spike, reduce forecasted peak by 10–15% and shift mean toward lower end.
